response.title: can a solar generator run a mini split in a tiny house
response.answer:
Yes, a solar generator can run a mini-split air conditioner in a tiny house, and it's actually one of the more energy-efficient ways to heat and cool a small space.

The key is choosing a solar generator with enough inverter power, battery capacity, and solar panel capacity.

For a typical 150–400 sq. ft. tiny house, a 9,000–12,000 BTU inverter mini-split is often a reasonable starting point, depending on insulation, climate, and window area.

These are illustrative operating ranges, not constant consumption. An inverter mini-split can use much less power once the house reaches the desired temperature.

2. What size solar generator do you need?

For a 9,000 BTU mini-split, here's a practical starting point:

4. What I would choose for a tiny house

markup:
**Yes, a solar generator can run a mini-split air conditioner in a tiny house**, and it's actually one of the more energy-efficient ways to heat and cool a small space.

The key is choosing a solar generator with enough **inverter power, battery capacity, and solar panel capacity**.

For a typical 150–400 sq. ft. tiny house, a 9,000–12,000 BTU inverter mini-split is often a reasonable starting point, depending on insulation, climate, and window area.

## 1. How much electricity does a mini-split use?

| Mini-split size | Typical running power | Energy used in 8 hours |
|---|---:|---:|
| 6,000 BTU | 300–600 W | 2.4–4.8 kWh |
| 9,000 BTU | 400–900 W | 3.2–7.2 kWh |
| 12,000 BTU | 500–1,200 W | 4–9.6 kWh |
| 18,000 BTU | 700–1,800 W | 5.6–14.4 kWh |

These are illustrative operating ranges, not constant consumption. An inverter mini-split can use much less power once the house reaches the desired temperature.

## 2. What size solar generator do you need?

For a 9,000 BTU mini-split, here's a practical starting point:

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Inverter output</text>
      <title size="xl">2,000 W+</title>
      <caption>Continuous AC output</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Battery storage</text>
      <title size="xl">5–10 kWh</title>
      <caption>For substantial overnight runtime</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Solar panels</text>
      <title size="xl">1.5–3 kW</title>
      <caption>For meaningful daily recharging</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Output voltage</text>
      <title size="xl">120/240 V</title>
      <caption>Must match your mini-split</caption>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
</box>

A 240V mini-split needs a generator that actually supplies compatible 240V power; a standard 120V portable power station won't run it directly.

## 3. How long will it run on battery?

Here's a calculator using a 9,000 BTU mini-split.

{@body const [battery,setBattery] = DIL.useState(5)}
{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(600)}
{@body const [solar,setSolar] = DIL.useState(2000)}
{@body const usable = battery*1000*0.85}
{@body const hours = usable/watts}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Battery capacity**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{battery} kWh</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={1} max={20} step={1} value={battery} onChange={setBattery}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Average mini-split consumption**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{watts} W</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={200} max={1500} step={100} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  <box background="surface-secondary" padding={3} radius="lg" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated battery-only runtime</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{hours.toFixed(1)} hours</title>
    <caption>Assumes 85% usable AC energy after losses, no solar charging, and constant average consumption.</caption>
  </box>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Installed solar panel capacity**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{solar.toLocaleString("en-US")} W</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={0} max={4000} step={250} value={solar} onChange={setSolar}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Estimated solar production per sunny day</text>
    **{(solar*4*0.75/1000).toFixed(1)} kWh**
  </row>
  <caption>Assumes 4 peak-sun-hours and 75% overall solar-system efficiency. Weather, shading, season and location will change production.</caption>
</box>

## 4. What I would choose for a tiny house

For an off-grid tiny house, I'd favor an efficient inverter mini-split, a 5–10 kWh expandable battery system, and enough panels to cover the daily energy demand.

Heating in winter can be considerably more demanding than cooling in summer, especially in cold climates. Proper heat-pump sizing and cold-weather performance are important. <Cite refs={["turn254056search2","turn254056search3"]}/>

**Three questions will help me size your setup:**

{@body const [area,setArea] = DIL.useState("200–400 sq ft")}
{@body const [purpose,setPurpose] = DIL.useState("Both heating and cooling")}
{@body const [setup,setSetup] = DIL.useState("Completely off-grid")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Size a solar generator and mini-split system for my tiny house. House size: "+area+". Use: "+purpose+". Power setup: "+setup+". Recommend battery kWh, inverter watts, solar panel watts, and expected runtime.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>How big is your tiny house?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={area} onChange={setArea}>
        <radio value="Under 200 sq ft">Under 200 sq. ft.</radio>

        <radio value="Over 600 sq ft">Over 600 sq. ft.</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>

        <radio value="Cooling only">Cooling only</radio>
        <radio value="Both heating and cooling">Both heating and cooling</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>

        <radio value="Completely off-grid">Completely off-grid</radio>
        <radio value="Grid-connected with solar backup">Grid-connected with solar backup</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Size my solar setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>
